title: Pregame line movement concentrates in the final hour (NBA most of all)
headline_insight: In the NBA, roughly a third of all pregame line movement lands in the final hour before tip -- final_hour_movement_share 0.3247, the highest of any measured sport.
what_it_means: The artifact records when movement occurred; it does not identify its cause. In the NBA the per-snapshot price motion inside the last hour (0-1h mean_abs_move 0.00117) is about seventeen times the size of the early-window motion (6h+ mean_abs_move 7e-05).
how_to_read: Bars are minutes-to-start buckets; height is the mean absolute devigged-probability move between consecutive snapshots, and final_hour_movement_share is the fraction of total absolute movement that happens in the last 60 minutes.
why_it_matters: The time-to-start buckets let readers compare an input timestamp with the published movement record without assigning a cause to that movement.
caveat: descriptive_only -- this is consecutive-snapshot movement from our own scraped line_history (min_moves_floor 20), a microstructure measurement, not a trading signal.
